evals.prompt: You are starting ticket PROJ-42 (add a webhook endpoint, consumed by the web client) on a repository other agents are also working on. Set up your environment, say what must exist before you and the frontend engineer can work in parallel, and describe what you will remove when done.
evals.expected_output: A worktree created from the project root at <project-root>/PROJ-42-<slug>, own Docker containers and LocalStack for the touched services, a database snapshot or seed, the API contract written first so the frontend mocks it while the backend returns labelled mock data, dependency shapes resolved before code, the app and tests run inside that environment, and the worktree, containers and snapshot removed after the PR is opened
expectations: The git worktree is created at the project root, never inside the harness's directory
Docker containers and LocalStack are started for the services touched and not reused from another agent
The database is snapshotted or seeded for this agent
The API contract is written before frontend and backend work in parallel; the frontend mocks it and the backend returns labelled mock data
Any dependency's shape and type is resolved before code is written against it
The app and tests run inside this environment
After opening the PR, the worktree, containers and snapshot are removed

evals.prompt: You are the mobile engineer on PROJ-77 and need an iOS and an Android release build. EAS reports 15 Android builds already used this month, and the iOS build has sat in the EAS queue for 40 minutes. A backend agent is already working on the one live dev machine. Say what you do.
evals.expected_output: Builds on EAS by default with eas-build.sh; Android falls back to AWS because the free builds are used up, iOS because the queue passed the limit and the EAS build is canceled, both recorded on the ticket; Android joins the live dev machine if cloud-capacity shows headroom (else launches the default m8i.2xlarge within the machine cap) and builds in Docker in its own work directory; iOS reuses a free Mac host or asks for a new one stating the 24-hour minimum; artifacts copied back; cloud-down removes only its own directory and leaves the backend agent's machine running; cloud-reap at start and end
expectations: Uses EAS Build first and falls back to AWS only for the stated reasons (free builds used up, queue wait over the limit), recording each on the ticket
Checks the live machine's headroom from its metrics before joining it, and launches another default machine only when it has none
Does not launch a type other than m8i.2xlarge, or a new Mac host, without the user's explicit permission; states the 24-hour minimum for a Mac host
Works in its own ~/work directory and Compose project without touching the backend agent's directory, containers, or ports
cloud-down.sh removes only its own work and does not terminate a machine another agent is still on
Copies no local AWS credentials or tokens to the machine
If an EAS build fails, reads the logs and reports the reason; does not move it to AWS or local without the user deciding
